paper.title: Learning to Bid in Contextual First Price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Binary feedback with known noise distribution (contextual first price auctions)
unmapped: Repeated first-price auction: learner bids b_t in [0,1] with known value beta_0(x_t); utility (beta_0(x_t)-b)F(b - alpha_0.x_t)
Competing max bid m_t = alpha_0.x_t + z_t, alpha_0 unknown with ||alpha_0||_1 <= W (W known)
Noise distribution F known, log-concave differentiable density
settings.definition_quote: Binary feedback: the learner only observes the indicator $\delta_t = \1\{b_t \geq m_t\}$. ... $m_t = \langle \alpha_0, x_t \rangle + z_t$, where $z_t$ i.i.d sampled from an unknown mean zero distribution $\F$ and $W$ is a publicly known parameter.

settings.name_in_paper: Binary feedback with partially-known noise distribution
unmapped: Repeated contextual first-price auction with linear competing-bid model m_t = alpha_0.x_t + z_t, ||alpha_0||_1 <= W (W known)
Noise is a known zero-mean log-concave base distribution F_0 scaled by unknown sigma (|1/sigma| <= W)
Bids restricted to be at least a minimum bid Delta; benchmark is the optimal policy truncated at Delta
settings.definition_quote: we extend to the case that the noise distribution $\F$ is parameterized by a zero-mean base noise distribution $\F_0$ and a variance $\sigma^2 (\sigma > 0)$, where $\F_{0}$ is known (e.g. $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$) but $\sigma$ is unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Full information feedback model with unknown noise distribution
unmapped: Repeated contextual first-price auction with linear competing-bid model m_t = alpha_0.x_t + z_t, ||alpha_0||_1 <= W (W known)
Noise distribution unknown, only known to have log-concave density; learner observes m_t each round
Learner uses density upper bound B_2 in the estimator
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider the full information feedback model with unknown noise distribution, i.e., the learner has no information of noise distribution, however she can always observe the highest bid of all other bidders $m_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Full information feedback with known Gaussian noise (lower bound)
unmapped: Repeated contextual first-price auction with linear competing-bid model m_t = alpha_0.x_t + z_t, ||alpha_0||_1 <= W
Noise z_t ~ N(0, sigma^2), sigma known; m_t observed each round
settings.definition_quote: For any $T$, we assume that the market value $z_t, 1 \leq t \leq T$ are fully observed. We further assume $z_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$, where $\sigma$ is known.

algorithms.name: Bidding algorithm in the binary feedback model with known noise distribution (Algorithm 1, episodic MLE)
Bidding algorithm in the binary feedback model with partially-known noise distribution (Algorithm 2)
Bidding algorithm in the full information feedback model with unknown noise distribution (Algorithm 3, log-concave density estimator + MLE)

conditions: Assumption 2.2: noise density f differentiable and log-concave
Assumption 2.3: B_1 <= f(x) <= B_2 and f'(x) <= B_3 on [-W, 1+W]

source.label: thm:binary-known-noise-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assump:bounded-noise} and Assumption~\ref{assump:log-concave} hold, setting $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret achieved in the binary feedback model with known noise distribution is at most $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ omits $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Õ hides log log T only; constants depend on W, B_2, B_3, h_W, l_W. Regret is defined as an expectation of utility differences but stated to hold w.p. 1-delta (over the estimation). Binary win/lose feedback mapped to partial_monitoring. Compute: convex MLE solvable by gradient descent.

conditions: Assumptions 2.2 and 2.3 (log-concave differentiable density, bounded density/derivative on [-W,1+W])
Assumption 3.1: max eigenvalue of Sigma=E[x x^T] <= lambda_1, min eigenvalue >= lambda_2 > 0, Sigma - E[x]E[x]^T > lambda_3 I
Bids and benchmark truncated below at minimum bid Delta > 0

source.label: thm:regret-binary-partial-known-noise
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assump:log-concave},~\ref{assump:bounded-noise} and~\ref{assump:eigenvalue-ub} hold, setting $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret (w.r.t the benchmark defined in Eq.~(\ref{eq:opt-bid-binary-partial-known-noise})) achieved in the binary feedback model with partially known noise distribution is bounded by $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ ignores $\log T$ and $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Benchmark is the optimal clairvoyant policy truncated at Delta. Proof gives O(log log T sqrt(log(d log log T/delta) T)).

conditions: Assumptions 2.2 and 2.3 (log-concave differentiable density, bounded density/derivative on [-W,1+W])
Assumption 3.1 (footnote: only min eigenvalue of Sigma >= lambda_2 > 0 needed)

source.label: thm:full-info-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assump:log-concave},~\ref{assump:bounded-noise}, and~\ref{assump:eigenvalue-ub} hold, and $T$ is sufficiently large. Given $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots,$ then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret is bounded by $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{d\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ ignores $\log T$ and $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Paper explicitly leaves computational efficiency open. Õ hides log T and log log T.

conditions: Only for bidding policies in class Pi: b_t = max{0, alpha_t.x_t + phi^{-1}(beta_0(x_t) - alpha_t.x_t)} with alpha_t H_{t-1}-measurable and ||alpha_t||_1 <= W
Contexts with coordinates i.i.d. uniform on {-1,1} (in the proof)
Noise z_t ~ N(0, sigma^2) with sigma known; m_t fully observed

source.label: thm:lower-bound-known-F
source.quote: For any $T$, we assume that the market value $z_t, 1 \leq t \leq T$ are fully observed. We further assume $z_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$, where $\sigma$ is known. Let $\Pi$ be the set of bidding polices $\pi$ defined in Eq.~(\ref{eq:bidding-policy}), then any bidding policy $\pi$ must incur expected regret $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Proof ends with Omega(sqrt(T log T)), but statement says Omega(sqrt T); recorded the statement. Regret is expected utility difference against the clairvoyant bid (pseudo-regret style).

cited_results.setting_description: Contextual pricing with binary feedback, known log-concave noise distribution, sparse parameter (sparsity s_0) and bounded eigenvalues of Sigma
